app.title: River Outlook: synthetic river-flow records and design flows
app.summary: A person chooses how many years of synthetic monthly flow to generate and how many independent records to make, using presets or typed values, and presses generate. The interface builds the records from a time-series model fitted ahead of time, shows the first record as an undated year-by-month table, and offers it as a CSV download. From all the records together it ranks the annual maxima to give a design flow for each return period, with a table and a chart. It then compares the synthetic and measured records with a histogram, a flow-duration curve and summary statistics, and an expandable section shows the model's coefficients, its seasonal parameters and how it did on held-out data.

task.text: Generate long synthetic monthly flow records from a fitted stochastic model and read off design flows for a set of return periods, checking that the synthetic record behaves like the measured one.

data.text: A measured monthly river-discharge record, and model coefficients fitted to it ahead of time, from which synthetic monthly records of any length are generated.
data.item: one month's discharge value in a measured or synthetic record

stage.text: generating synthetic flow records from a fitted model to estimate design flows, before sizing structures

mechanism.text: A control panel sets the record length and the number of records, and pressing generate fills the centre with the record table, a return-period table and chart, and plots comparing the measured and synthetic distributions. Beside these, a right rail sets summary statistics for the synthetic record against the same statistics for the measured one, and an expander holds the model's coefficients and its validation.

field.text: stochastic generation of streamflow with ARIMA models, and flood frequency analysis, in hydrology

workflow.name: simulate long records from a fitted model and read off design values

steps.here: Preset buttons (30, 100, 500 or 1,000 years) or a number input set the record length, and a second input sets how many independent records to make. A caption shows the total number of synthetic years.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: 'Generate synthetic record' rebuilds the ARIMA model from coefficients saved in a results file and simulates deseasonalised log flows with bootstrapped residuals, then restores the seasonal cycle and undoes the log transform.
The first record is shown as a table of numbered years and months with a discharge column. Years are numbered, not dated.
A download button saves the record as a CSV named by its length.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Annual maxima are pooled across all records and ranked, giving a design flow for each return period from 2 to 500 years. These appear in a table and on a log-scale chart, with the largest measured month drawn as a dashed line.

Measured and synthetic records are overlaid as a histogram and as flow-duration curves. Side cards compare the mean, the extremes, percentiles and the standard deviation, and a pill shows how many held-out properties the model reproduced.

An expander 'For the curious' shows the coefficients with standard errors, the twelve monthly seasonal parameters, a comparison of standardisation with lag-12 differencing, stationarity tests, and a table of held-out properties marked as reproduced or not.

distinctive: The output is an undated synthetic record, not a forecast: years are numbered 1 to N because the process is stationary.
Return periods with fewer synthetic years than their length are dropped from the table.
Several independent records are pooled, so the design flows rest on many more annual maxima than the measured record has.
The design-flow chart marks the largest month ever measured, so the person can see how far past the record each estimate reaches.
Validation counts how many hydrological properties of a held-out period fall inside the 90% range of the simulated records, and the count is shown as a track-record rating.
